attempts.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as a DHCP relay between two isolated L2 segments — eth1 (192.168.10.0/24, toward node2) and eth2 (192.168.20.0/24, toward node3) — using the platform's own docker-dhcp-relay image invoked directly (dhcrelay -i eth2 -i eth1 192.168.10.2), persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d for the IPs and docker restart-policy=unless-stopped for the relay container. Installed and configured isc-dhcp-server (package "dhcp") on node2, binding to eth1 with subnet declarations for both the local segment and node3's subnet (192.168.20.0/24, range .100-.200). Diagnosed and fixed a routing gap where node2's DHCPOFFER (destined to node1's giaddr 192.168.20.1) had no route and fell through the default gateway; added a static route via node1's eth1. Verified node3 obtains a real DHCP lease (192.168.20.100/24) from node2's service through node1's relay via NetworkManager. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, capturing pre/post boot_id changes and confirming the DHCP-relay path, lease data, and SONiC container stack fully recovered after each reboot (node3 automatically re-obtained its lease after its own reboot).
